title: consolidate-toolcache-and-staged-presubmit-profiles
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: The presubmit layer has accumulated several independent bootstraps (bash scripts, per-language tool installers and ad-hoc caches) that increase CI setup time and flakiness. This change consolidates the on-runner toolcache manifest into a single typed cache registry, replaces brittle shell bootstraps with a small idempotent Go toolcache binary, and stages presubmit profiles so fast feedback lanes use a narrow toolchain while full presubmit uses the broader manifest.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Consolidate toolcache manifests, add typed presubmit profiles (fast/smoke/full), replace bootstrap.sh with tools/toolcache/bootstrap (Go), introduce a lightweight presubmit cache priming step and a dep-pruner that removes transitive devdeps from the CI image layer.

Checklist: - [x] Add typed toolcache manifest and merge loader - [x] Implement idempotent Go bootstrap with hermetic installs - [x] Stage presubmit profiles and document usage in .github/README-presubmit.md - [x] Add cache-priming action to short feedback lanes - [x] Add dep-pruner hook that runs in image build step - [x] Add migration notes and automated compat shim for existing runners - [x] CI green on linux/amd64 and macos/arm64 matrices

Commits summary: single squash with earlier feature commits. Major logical commits: initial typed manifest schema, go bootstrap implementation, presubmit profile wiring, cache-priming action, dep-pruner integration, docs and migration notes.

Files changed (high level): - .github/workflows/presubmit-fast.yml: new staged workflow that runs the cache-priming step and fast lint/test profile - .github/workflows/presubmit-full.yml: full suite wired to the consolidated manifest - ci/toolcache/manifest.yaml: new typed manifest for tools per-platform and profile hints - tools/toolcache/bootstrap/main.go: idempotent bootstrap binary (replace scripts/bootstrap.sh) - scripts/bootstrap.sh: removed and replaced with compat shim that invokes the new binary - ci/docker/dep-pruner: small script that strips transitive devdeps during image build - .github/README-presubmit.md: docs for fast/smoke/full profiles and migration steps

Why this is safe: The Go bootstrap is idempotent and uses the same tool download URLs as the previous scripts; a compat shim leaves the old script path as a thin wrapper to the new binary to avoid breaking older runners. Toolcache manifest includes schema versioning so future rollouts can do staged flips. The presubmit staging only affects which profile runs on a given workflow; it does not change main branch protections.

Operational notes: - Rollout plan: merge to main and enable the fast presubmit lane by default; monitor presubmit latency and cache hit rates for two weeks. - Metric targets: reduce presubmit setup time 30% on average, increase toolcache hit rate to >90% for common devtools. - Fallback: old bootstrap shim remains; infra can flip a feature flag in the manifest loader to revert to per-repo scripts.

CI summary: First run failed on macos/arm64 due to a permission edge-case in the Go binary; second run added proper umask handling and all matrix lanes passed. Full check suite shows lint/test coverage unchanged.

Migration: - For self-hosted runners: run tools/toolcache/bootstrap --migrate to populate the new cache layout. - For release automation agents: the manifest loader exposes an env var TOOLCACHE_MANIFEST that can point to a pinned manifest for deterministic builds.

Related work: ENG-4128 consolidates tool manifests across repos; ENG-4151 defines presubmit profiles for staged feedback. SUP-3221 tracked increased CI runtime during a support incident and motivated this optimization.

Notes for reviewers: look at the bootstrapping semantics in main.go for idempotence, confirm manifest schema covers all platform/tool combos we use, and verify the presubmit profile wiring does not accidentally widen fast lanes.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after two approving reviews and CI green. There is a brief post-merge rollout step to enable the cache-priming action; infra ops toggled the manifest loader flag to live on 2026-01-28.
commits: feat(ci): add typed toolcache manifest and loader
feat(ci): implement idempotent Go bootstrap for runner toolcache
chore(ci): stage presubmit profiles (fast/smoke/full) and wire workflows
feat(ci): add cache-priming action for fast feedback lanes
chore(docker): integrate dep-pruner into CI image build
review_thread: Diego Alvarez (requested changes): Can you add unit tests for the manifest loader schema parsing? The manifest currently allows optional 'profile' hints but the loader silently ignores unknown fields.

Maya Chen (author): Added schema tests and explicit unknown-field rejection; loader now returns an error when encountering unknown top-level keys (will be backwards-compatible by guarding on schema_version).
Priya Natarajan (comment): The Go bootstrap writes to /tmp/toolcache during install; can we ensure it handles concurrent runs on shared runners?
Maya Chen (reply): The bootstrap now creates a lockfile under TOOLCACHE_DIR/.lock and retries with exponential backoff for 30s; added integration test that spawns concurrent bootstraps.
Liam O'Connor (approval): Verified presubmit-fast latency improvement in sandbox, cache hit exporter metrics look good. Approving.
CI Bot (status): macos/arm64 failed on first run - permission fix applied; subsequent run passed all checks.
release_notes: Consolidated CI toolcache into a typed manifest, added an idempotent Go bootstrap, introduced staged presubmit profiles (fast/smoke/full), added cache-priming action and dep-pruner for CI image builds. Expected to reduce presubmit setup time and CI flakiness.
notes_for_ops: Enable cache-priming action for fast lanes via feature flag in the manifest loader. Monitor metric ci.presubmit.setup_time and ci.toolcache.hit_rate for two weeks. Migration command: tools/toolcache/bootstrap --migrate.
testing_notes: Unit tests for manifest parsing added. Integration test for concurrent bootstrap added. Manual sandbox validated presubmit-fast end-to-end and metrics. CI matrix passed on second run.
